notes.h: Why national agencies oversee food safety
notes.b: Consumers cannot see how hygienically their food was produced, so the state sets up bodies to check it on their behalf. In Ireland one central body coordinates the system and other bodies do the inspecting.
points: National agencies protect consumers by setting and enforcing food safety standards, inspecting food businesses, testing food and acting when food is unsafe.
Food businesses must be monitored independently, because a business cannot be relied on to judge its own hygiene and customers have no way of checking it themselves.
An outbreak or contamination can cross counties and countries, so a national system is needed to trace it and respond quickly.
The Irish system has one central body, the Food Safety Authority of Ireland (FSAI), which coordinates, and a group of official agencies that carry out the inspecting.
notes.tip: Say that the FSAI coordinates and the official agencies inspect. Do not say the FSAI inspects every premises itself.

notes.h: Food Safety Authority of Ireland (Higher Level only)
notes.b: The FSAI is the state body at the centre of food safety in Ireland. It sets the direction and coordinates the work, while others carry out most of the inspections.
points: The Food Safety Authority of Ireland (FSAI) is the state body responsible for food safety in Ireland, established under the Food Safety Authority of Ireland Act 1998.

The FSAI operates under the Department of Health, the government department responsible for health policy. The FSAI advises the Minister on food safety, but the Department itself does not inspect food premises.
It co-ordinates the enforcement of food safety legislation in Ireland, working through the official agencies, and it audits their work rather than inspecting most premises itself.
It protects consumers by ensuring that food is safe to eat and that food information is accurate.

It works with food businesses to make sure food is produced safely, for example through guidance and training on hygiene and HACCP systems (the system of identifying and controlling hazards in food production).
It takes action, through the agencies, when a food premises is in breach of food regulations, because it is the agencies that can inspect and enforce on the ground.
notes.tip: For an outline of the FSAI, give three clear points such as coordinating enforcement, advising the Minister and protecting consumers, or working with industry on HACCP. Do not say it inspects premises or issues licences, because the official agencies inspect.

notes.h: Other FSAI roles and what it does not do (Higher Level only)
notes.b: Beyond coordinating enforcement, the FSAI informs the public, handles emergencies and processes applications for new food products. It has one clear limit: it is about safety, not promotion.
points: It gives consumers and food businesses authoritative advice and publishes food safety information, so that both groups can rely on one trusted source.
It carries out scientific work, which gives its advice and decisions an evidence base.
It processes applications for novel foods and for new methods of food processing, so that new products are assessed before they reach consumers.
It also handles food alerts, product withdrawals and recalls, works with the agencies on traceability and leads on food incidents.
It does not promote Irish food at home or abroad; that is the role of Bord Bia (the Irish Food Board), which is why an exam statement that the FSAI promotes Irish food is false.
notes.tip: Do not mix up the FSAI (safe food, the law) with Bord Bia (promoting Irish food).

notes.h: Official agencies under contract to the FSAI (Higher Level only)
notes.b: The FSAI does not carry out most food controls itself. Official agencies do this work under service contracts with the FSAI, which means the FSAI can coordinate one national system without employing every inspector.
points: The official agencies are the Health Service Executive (HSE), the Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine, the Sea-Fisheries Protection Authority and the local authorities.
Official agencies carry out inspections, sampling and analysis of food in the places they cover, and they enforce the rules on the FSAI's behalf.
The Sea-Fisheries Protection Authority carries out the official food safety controls on fish and shellfish, from production and landing through processing to distribution, but not retail.
Local authorities carry out food controls under contract to the FSAI in their own areas, mainly veterinary inspections of food premises that handle meat and other animal products.
notes.tip: Use the current name, Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine. Do not use the older names for the Department or the Regional Health Boards.

notes.h: Health Service Executive: Environmental Health Service (Higher Level only)
notes.b: The HSE is the national health service, and its Environmental Health Service does most of the day-to-day inspection of food premises. Its staff are environmental health officers, who work for the HSE and not for the FSAI.
points: Environmental health officers (EHOs), working in the HSE's Environmental Health Service, carry out the inspections of food premises, including restaurants, cafés, shops, hospital kitchens, manufacturers and wholesalers.
The service registers new food premises, so that every business handling food is known to the authorities before it starts trading.
It inspects food premises and farms.
It handles hygiene complaints and issues closure orders and enforcement notices where food premises are unsafe, which stops a risky business from continuing to sell food.
It ensures food safety at public gatherings and events.
It monitors compliance with food, labelling, additives and contaminants legislation, and takes samples of food for testing.
It responds to rapid alerts and recalls, and it investigates food poisoning outbreaks.
It educates and advises food businesses on compliance with the law.
notes.tip: A question on the HSE or the EHO is worth a full list of roles. Cover registering premises, inspecting premises such as hospital kitchens, restaurants, shops and manufacturers, complaints and closure orders, public gatherings, monitoring the law, alerts and recalls, and education. Do not say the EHO works for the FSAI.

notes.b: Inspectors can see a kitchen, but only a laboratory can tell what is in a food. The Public Analyst Laboratories provide that testing, and they analyse rather than inspect.
points: The Public Analyst Laboratories are run by the HSE.
They analyse food and water, including samples taken by environmental health officers.
They test food for compliance with food law and labelling law, for example its composition, additives, contaminants and microbiological quality (the bacteria in it).
They test samples submitted by members of the public, for a fee.
Their results help ensure that food sold to consumers is safe and wholesome, and they give the evidence needed for legal action.
notes.tip: For the role of the laboratories, give three points: they analyse food and water, they test compliance with food and labelling law, and they test public samples for a fee. Do not give them an inspection role.

notes.h: Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine (Higher Level only)
notes.b: This Department looks after food at the farm end of the food chain, where animals and animal products come from. Its controls follow food from the farm to the shop.
points: It monitors food safety in meat and meat products, milk and milk products, and eggs and egg products.
It monitors the use of pesticides in food production, so that residues (traces left on or in food) do not reach consumers.
It enforces EU controls on the import of animal-based foods from countries outside the EU.
It is responsible for the registration and traceability of cattle, pigs and sheep, so that an animal can be traced if a problem is found.
It ensures correct hygiene procedures are followed from the dairy farm, to the dairy, through to the retailer and the consumer.
notes.tip: For this Department give separate points such as monitoring meat, dairy, eggs and pesticides, import controls, animal registration and traceability, and hygiene from farm to consumer.

notes.h: How the agencies work together (Higher Level only)
notes.b: Because the inspecting is shared between several bodies, they need common ways of tracking and removing unsafe food. The FSAI coordinates all of these.
points: The FSAI and the official agencies work together on inspections, sampling, alerts, product withdrawals and recalls.
Traceability allows an unsafe product to be traced back to its supplier (one step back) and forward to the businesses that received it (one step forward).
A product withdrawal removes a product from the supply chain, whereas a product recall also collects it from consumers by asking them to return it.
Rapid alerts pass warnings about unsafe food quickly to the agencies that must act on them, so that action can be taken before more people are harmed.

keyTerms.definition: The state body responsible for food safety in Ireland, which co-ordinates food safety enforcement and advises consumers and food businesses.
A body, such as the HSE or a local authority, that carries out food controls under contract to the FSAI.
An officer of the HSE's Environmental Health Service who inspects food premises and investigates hygiene complaints.
A laboratory run by the HSE that analyses food and water to check that they are safe and comply with the law.
An order that closes a food premises, issued by the Environmental Health Service when the premises is unsafe.
A warning about an unsafe food that is passed quickly to the agencies that must act on it.
The removal of an unsafe product from the supply chain, before it reaches consumers.
The collection of an unsafe product from consumers who have already bought it.
The ability to trace a food back to its supplier and forward to the businesses that received it.

factCards.term: Department that the FSAI operates under
Four official agencies that carry out food controls under contract to the FSAI
factCards.definition: The HSE, the Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine, the Sea-Fisheries Protection Authority and the local authorities.

factCards.term: Four functions of the Public Analyst Laboratories
factCards.definition: Analysing food and water; testing compliance with food and labelling law; testing public samples for a fee; and ensuring that food is safe and wholesome.

factCards.term: Three functions of the Environmental Health Service in food safety
factCards.definition: Registering new food premises; inspecting food premises and farms; and handling hygiene complaints and issuing closure orders.

factCards.term: Three functions of the Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine in food safety
factCards.definition: Monitoring meat, milk and egg products and pesticide use; enforcing EU controls on imports of animal-based foods from outside the EU; and registering and tracing cattle, pigs and sheep.

factCards.term: Which body promotes Irish food, drink and horticulture
factCards.definition: Bord Bia (the Irish Food Board), not the FSAI.

factCards.term: Two things the FSAI gives consumers and food businesses
factCards.definition: Authoritative advice, and published food safety information.

questions.prompt: Identify two official agencies that carry out food controls under contract to the FSAI, and state one food safety function of each.
questions.model: Health Service Executive: its Environmental Health Service registers new food premises and inspects them, or handles hygiene complaints and issues closure orders. Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine: monitors food safety in meat, milk and egg products, or enforces EU controls on imports of animal-based foods from outside the EU. Other accepted agencies include the Sea-Fisheries Protection Authority, which controls fish and shellfish safety, and local authorities, which carry out food controls in their areas.

questions.prompt: Discuss how the FSAI and the official agencies work together to protect consumers from unsafe food.
questions.model: The FSAI operates under the Department of Health and co-ordinates the enforcement of food safety legislation, advising the Minister and ensuring that food is safe and honestly labelled. Official agencies carry out the controls under contract: the HSE's Environmental Health Service inspects food premises, registers new premises, handles hygiene complaints and issues closure orders; Public Analyst Laboratories analyse food and water and test compliance with food and labelling law; the Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine monitors meat, milk, egg products and pesticide use and controls imports from outside the EU; the Sea-Fisheries Protection Authority controls fish and shellfish; local authorities carry out controls in their areas. Together they use inspections and sampling, and work on rapid alerts, traceability, product withdrawals and recalls, so that unsafe food is removed from sale quickly and consumers are advised.
